method: YouTube ids taken from youtube.com search-result pages fetched this session; each verified via oEmbed (HTTP 200) and the watch page (playableInEmbed, isLiveContent, lengthSeconds). startAt estimated from the first YouTube storyboard sheet (one frame per 10 s) - not from watching with sound. File refs are Wikimedia Commons 480p VP9 transcodes taken from the videoinfo derivatives API and HEAD-checked; licence from Commons extmetadata.

candidates.title: Dog TV Daycare for Tuesdays
candidates.why: Dogs were the top-ranked screen subject in Donohue et al. 2024 (93% of watchers) and the most-watched test clip; close, dog-height play with real barking is the strongest attention-getter but the uploader itself warns of overstimulation.
candidates.notes: Storyboard: dogs on screen from ~10 s.

candidates.title: Dog Park TV Saturday afternoon in the Dog Zone
candidates.why: Real dog-park footage of conspecifics moving across frame, matching the conspecific + horizontal-movement criteria used for the Wisconsin test videos.
candidates.notes: Title cards for first ~20 s, then a quiet stretch of open field; action density in first 80 s is low - consider a later startAt after manual review.

candidates.title: Dog park at Bluff creek Los Angeles , relaxing ASMR 4K
candidates.why: Conspecifics in social play with ambient sound; dogs gaze longer at social-interaction scenes than non-social ones (Tornqvist et al. 2015).
candidates.notes: First ~50 s is an empty park walk-in; dogs from ~60 s. Handheld camera.

candidates.title: Dog TV - Dogs playing in the dog park
candidates.why: Low, static camera on a few dogs playing close to the lens - conspecifics large on screen with lateral movement.
candidates.notes: Black frame at 0 s; play from ~10 s.

candidates.title: Dog Beach - 2 Hour Slow TV
candidates.why: Locked-off wide shot with many dogs running horizontally through frame: static camera + horizontal subject motion are exactly the Wisconsin stimulus-selection criteria.
candidates.notes: Title text at 10-20 s and sparse beach in first minute; dogs are small in frame (letterboxed ultra-wide). Better on a big screen than a phone.

candidates.title: Daycare for Dogs 🐾 Calm Pack Walks | 12 Hours of Dog TV
candidates.channel: Tv for dogs, brought to you by Doggy Woods Retreat
candidates.why: Conspecifics at dog height walking calmly - keeps the top-ranked stimulus class (dogs) while avoiding chase/bark triggers.
candidates.notes: Episode title overlay at ~10 s. Audio not reviewed.

candidates.title: Take a 12 hour pack walk with your dog through the forest at Doggy Woods Retreat!  Filmed for dogs!
candidates.channel: Tv for dogs, brought to you by Doggy Woods Retreat
candidates.why: Pack of dogs filmed from dog height in forest; conspecific content with movement.
candidates.notes: Heavy on-screen text for roughly the first 80+ s (the text itself says barking and human voices are audible) - start later.

candidates.title: [NO ADS] Dog TV for Dogs to Watch 🐕 Virtual Dog Walk with Nature Sounds 🌲 Videos for Dogs
candidates.channel: Harmony Hounds - Relaxing Music for Dogs
candidates.why: Low-arousal filler: forward-motion woodland walk with a dog intermittently ahead; movement was the most-cited attractant (90% of owners) but there is no prey/alarm trigger.
candidates.notes: Black frame at 0 s. Has calming music per description, not pure natural sound.

candidates.title: TheDogCam | 10hrs of Mountain Lake Virtual Dog Walks In The Swiss Alps 🐾🌊 GoPro DogTV
candidates.why: Dog's-eye GoPro view with the dog's head in frame and continuous forward motion; calm conspecific content.
candidates.notes: Text overlays during at least the first 80 s; humans frequently in frame.

candidates.title: GoPro Dog Plays Fetch In River- Take A Ride On Golden Retrievers Back
candidates.why: Dog-back POV fetch in a river: toy-chase from the dog's perspective with splashing sound; action from the first seconds.
candidates.notes: Very shaky camera; dog's back fills part of the frame. 25 min.

candidates.title: Dog TV Videos ~ Beautiful Calming Sheep Videos and Sounds ⭐ 8 HOURS of TV for Dogs ⭐
candidates.why: Livestock interested 64% of watcher dogs in Donohue et al. 2024; grazing sheep with bleats give animal content at low speed.
candidates.notes: Sheep are distant until ~50 s. Herding breeds may fixate/stalk - treat as medium for them.

candidates.title: Best for Dogs: 10 hours of Red Squirrel Spectacular
candidates.why: Close-up squirrels with darting movement - squirrels interested 56% of watcher dogs and fast animate motion is a strong orienting cue, but this is prey-drive attention.
candidates.notes: Black frame + title overlay until ~40 s.

candidates.title: Dog TV - Chipmunks, Squirrels, and Birds in the Woods.
candidates.why: Macro chipmunks/squirrels filling the frame with quick stop-start motion - the classic small-prey pattern.
candidates.notes: Black frame at 0 s; chipmunk from ~10 s.

candidates.title: ✨10-hour Dog & Cat TV ✨ Bunnies 🐇, Squirrels 🐿& Birds 🐦 chase each other around the honeysuckles.
candidates.why: Static ground-level camera with rabbits and squirrels chasing each other: chasing motion patterns are preferentially looked at by dogs early in exposure (Abdai et al.).
candidates.notes: Animals are fairly small in frame.

candidates.title: Rabbit! Rabbit! Rabbit! - 10 Hour Video for Pets on the First of the Month - Aug 01, 2023
candidates.why: Close-up wild rabbits, chipmunks and jays; small-mammal content with mostly stationary feeding, so less chase-triggering than squirrel videos.
candidates.notes: Black frame at 0 s.

candidates.title: Cat TV ~ Mice in The Jerry Mouse Hole 🐭 8 HOURS 🐭 Videos for Cats
candidates.why: Mice dashing in and out of a hole against a plain floor: fast, erratic, screen-crossing small-prey motion with high figure-ground contrast. Made for cats; terriers likely to react strongly.
candidates.notes: Tagged 'squirrels' as nearest available tag (small rodents).

candidates.title: Videos for Dogs To Watch - Dog TV Videos of Birds and Squirrels for Separation Anxiety
candidates.why: Made-for-dogs close-ups of birds then squirrels on a stump with birdsong; action from frame 0.
candidates.notes: Same maker as two catalog entries but a different video.

candidates.title: Entertain Your Cat or Dog with Pet TV | Deer, Squirrel, Fox, and Birds All Come for a Visit
candidates.why: Fox (a canid) plus deer and squirrels at close range; wild animals interested 65% of watcher dogs in Donohue et al. 2024.
candidates.notes: Logo at 0 s; fox on the log at ~30-80 s, which is a strong opening.

candidates.title: Back Yard Chickens Continuous Footage! Rooster Crowing! Hens Clucking!
candidates.why: Ground-level flock of chickens filling the frame with constant movement and loud clucking/crowing from 0 s - animal motion plus animal sound together.
candidates.notes: Rooster crowing may trigger alert barking.

candidates.title: 👀Entertain your Cat & Dog = 10 HOURS of Baby Goats & Chickens | Dog TV 🐶 | Cat TV 😻| Pet Enrichment
candidates.why: Baby goats approach and sniff the lens (large animal faces on screen) with chickens moving behind.
candidates.notes: Wire fence in front of lens.

candidates.title: Horses ~ Extremely Satisfying Video of Horses Grazing ⭐ 8 HOURS ⭐
candidates.why: Horses interested 63% of watcher dogs in Donohue et al. 2024; slow grazing is a calm animal stimulus.
candidates.notes: Ponies are distant for the first ~2.5 min; closer from ~160 s.

candidates.title: 8 Hours of Close-up Birds feeding with Sound in 4K - NO Interruptions #CATTV
candidates.why: Very close feeder shots with birds landing/leaving; the hopping-bird clip was the second most-watched test video in Donohue et al. 2024 (~half of dogs).
candidates.notes: Black frame at 0 s. Note: the red cardinal is not a salient colour for dichromatic dogs.

candidates.title: Puppiesplaying-tokyoarea-jan7-2020
candidates.why: Short clip of a puppy play-wrestling; conspecific content from frame 0, silent so no bark trigger.
candidates.notes: No audio track. Pet-shop pen; the playmate is a kitten. 22 s - loop or use as a sting.

candidates.title: Dogs pulling a sled
candidates.why: Musher's-eye view of a dog team running - continuous conspecific locomotion without play-fighting or barking close-ups.
candidates.notes: Dogs are small/seen from behind.

candidates.title: African wild dogs (Lycaon pictus) playing
candidates.why: Canid social play; dogs attend most to dog-like animals and to social interaction.
candidates.notes: Not visually reviewed; 480p transcode is ~22 MB.

candidates.title: Black squirrel eating seeds
candidates.why: Dark squirrels on white snow = maximum luminance contrast (works for dichromats) with squirrel-squirrel chases.
candidates.notes: Source is only 640x480 and soft.

candidates.title: Many squirls eating seeds
candidates.why: Several squirrels at once - more simultaneous small-prey motion.
candidates.notes: Not visually reviewed; 480p transcode ~25 MB.

candidates.title: Curious Oregon squirrels (26288379860)
candidates.why: Ground squirrels darting at burrow mouths close to the lens from frame 0; US-government public domain.
candidates.notes: Ends with a BLM logo card for the last ~4 s - trim or stop at ~32 s.

candidates.title: Red Squirrel eats a nut
candidates.why: Frame-filling squirrel, but sitting and eating rather than darting - attention without much chase trigger.
candidates.notes: No audio track. Title text burned in during the first seconds.

candidates.title: Red squirrel (Sciurus vulgaris) in England
candidates.why: Two minutes of red squirrel footage by a prolific wildlife videographer.
candidates.notes: Not visually reviewed.
